current_direction_as_written.summary: Intent -> clarify -> GitNexus explore -> structure phases -> mutate Beads graph directly via bd create --parent/--deps (single bash invocation board) -> test-planning companion issues -> claim first issue.
sources: core docs/plans/xtpi-worktree-first-flow.md section 3 (canonical loop: bd update --claim / bd close --reason)
core docs/design/issuetracking.md (deferred design; issues as executable contracts, validator-gated dispatch)
key_mechanics: Board created in ONE scripted bash invocation: epic first and alone, then children with --parent in dependency order
Hierarchical IDs deterministic by creation order (<epic>.1, <epic>.2, ...); main sequencing edges wired inline at create time via --deps; post-hoc edges via typed bd dep add
--deps direction semantics: bare id / depends-on:id / blocked-by:id make THIS issue depend on id; blocks:id reverses
Draft capture mode: contract:draft label, real PROBLEM + rough SCOPE, explicit 'TBD — needs exploration' elsewhere; draft beads are undispatchable ('A draft bead cannot be dispatched.')
Verification chained on the same invocation: bd children, bd graph, bd dep cycles
7-section bead contract mandatory for every task and epic; template must stay mirrored with using-specialists SKILL.md

target_direction.summary: Intent -> authored ChainDefinition -> review/freeze -> ResolvedChain -> Beads materialization.

nearest_written_precursors_in_core_docs.quote: One canonical resolver must produce: selected template → resolved DAG → exact Specialist and dispatch flags → parent/coordinator assignment → expected notification or monitor behavior → typed result contract → eligible next transitions.
nearest_written_precursors_in_core_docs.quote2: Do not implement separate partial resolvers in Core, xtmux, Specialists, prompts, and Archon adapters.

nearest_written_precursors_in_core_docs.quote: This K2 slice proves the common shape with existing Pi and Claude launchers. It does not depend on ResolvedChain, specialists.execution.v1, the chain reducer, MCP, plugins, or a production Codex launcher.
issue contract → validator → specialist chain → evidence graph → review → merge/close
nearest_written_precursors_in_core_docs.quote2: 'ready' should not mean only “not blocked by deps”. It should mean the issue contract is specific enough to launch the right specialist chain.

target_direction.gap: No core doc describes the authored-ChainDefinition flow yet. The planning skill mutates Beads directly; issuetracking.md is explicitly deferred; substrate canon holds resolved_chain_json as completeness contract. The freeze gate concept exists in three unconnected places: planning skill's bd set-state contract=ready promotion, issuetracking.md contract_status=ready verdict, substrate resolved_chain_json.

mechanics_worth_preserving.name: rich self-contained contracts
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_planning: The seven sections — `PROBLEM / SUCCESS / SCOPE / NON_GOALS / CONSTRAINTS / VALIDATION / OUTPUT` — are mandatory for every task and every epic.
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_quality_bar: The test of a good issue: could another agent pick it up cold and succeed?
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_drift_guard: Any drift between this template and the using-specialists contract creates partial contracts and weakens downstream specialist output.

mechanics_worth_preserving.name: hierarchy first
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote: Create the epic first, alone, and capture its ID ... Create every child with --parent "$EPIC" inside the same invocation, in dependency order — the issue that others wait on is created first.
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote2: Hierarchical IDs are assigned deterministically by creation order

mechanics_worth_preserving.name: dependencies separate (typed edges, inline where possible)
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote: `blocks` is only for hard must-happen-before sequencing; overusing it makes `bd ready` untrustworthy and hides review/test/follow-up meaning.
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote2: Companion test/reviewer/sanity/security issues should usually use `validates`, not `blocks`.
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote3: Follow-up issues spawned by exploration or review should use `discovered-from`, not `blocks`.

mechanics_worth_preserving.name: test-planning integration
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_planning_skill: After the implementation issues are created, invoke **test-planning**
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_test_triggers: Activates at three points: (1) issue-board creation from a spec/plan, (2) specialist-chain test authoring after executor/debugger work clarifies what changed, and (3) implementation closure to close coverage gaps.
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_batching: Don't create one test issue per implementation issue — that's overhead. Batch by layer and phase
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_gating: Test issues should gate the next phase of work. Use bd dependencies or document in the issue description

mechanics_worth_preserving.name: critical-path testing
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote: Do not frame test issues around coverage percentages. Frame them around critical paths and risk rationale.
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote2: a 90% line-coverage number says nothing about whether the one path that processes payments is tested. A critical path map forces explicit reasoning about what matters and what was skipped.
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote3: Static gates like `pyright`, `tsc`, `ruff`, ESLint, or schema validation are valuable, but they are not substitutes for smoke/E2E evidence.

mechanics_worth_preserving.name: file collision planning
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_scope: SCOPE — Files, symbols, modules this task MAY touch. Be explicit — file:line or symbol-list when possible.
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_boundary: Forbidden boundary ("do NOT touch") goes in NON_GOALS or CONSTRAINTS.
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_merge_rule: If two tasks always ship together → merge them

mechanics_worth_preserving.name: handoff quality
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote: Include a short **Architecture & Impact Summary** in your handoff message: Key execution flows/processes involved; Top d=1 dependents to watch; Highest observed risk (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL); Whether GitNexus-first or fallback exploration was used
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_self_check: [ ] First implementation issue is ready to claim
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote_observability_contract: Every implementation plan must include a logging/telemetry contract and an integration validation contract. Do this during planning, not as a reviewer afterthought.

mechanics_worth_preserving.name: draft capture honesty (intake for future ChainDefinition authoring)
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote: No one-liners, ever — draft mode included. PROBLEM must be real prose, SCOPE must be a real guess, and every other section must explicitly say `TBD — needs exploration` rather than being silently absent.
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote2: Draft mode defers the work, not the eventual rigor.

mechanics_worth_preserving.name: recent-work check before planning
mechanics_worth_preserving.quote: Stale mental models are the largest single source of over-scoping ... If a recent PR already did what the request is asking for, STOP and confirm with the operator before continuing.
